evals.name: clean-match-permitting-portal
evals.prompt:
We're going to bid on this one. Can you put together our proposal? Here's what they sent:

---
CITY OF WESTBROOK — REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL
RFP No. WB-2026-031: Online Permitting and Licensing Portal
Issued: January 12, 2026 | Questions due: January 22, 2026
Proposals due: February 11, 2026, 5:00 PM | Award: March 4, 2026 | Start: March 18, 2026

The City of Westbrook (population 96,000) seeks a vendor to deliver a public-facing portal for building permits, business licenses, and code-enforcement service requests. Today residents and contractors must visit the Permit Center in person; staff track applications on paper and in a shared spreadsheet. Average building-permit turnaround is 27 business days.

Requirements:
1. Online application submission for permits and licenses, with document upload
2. Applicant status tracking and email/SMS notification of status changes
3. Configurable staff review and approval routing across departments
4. Online fee payment with receipts
5. Public dashboard showing application volumes and average processing times
6. Integration with our Esri ArcGIS parcel data
7. Integration with our Tyler Technologies financial system for fee posting
8. Single sign-on for staff via our existing Okta tenant
9. Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 AA conformance
10. Retention of application records per state schedule (7 years)

Estimated budget: $450,000 - $900,000.

Evaluation: Technical approach 30, Relevant municipal experience 25, Cost 20, Team 15, Timeline 10.

Submit to Ms. Rhonda Pike, Procurement Manager, quoting RFP No. WB-2026-031.
---
evals.expected_output: A complete proposal in Markdown plus a rendered PDF, matched to the constituent-portal offering, addressing all 10 requirements and naming ArcGIS/Tyler/Okta specifically, priced as a fixed fee inside $450k-$900k, quoting RFP No. WB-2026-031 and addressed to Rhonda Pike.
assertions: Matches the request to the constituent-portal offering (permitting/licensing portal), not a generic custom web app
Addresses all 10 numbered requirements from the RFP
Names the buyer's actual systems by name: Esri ArcGIS, Tyler Technologies, and Okta
Quotes the buyer's reference number RFP No. WB-2026-031
Cover letter is addressed to Rhonda Pike
States a fixed fee that falls inside the stated budget of $450,000-$900,000
Addresses Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 AA conformance
Visibly addresses each of the 5 stated evaluation criteria (technical approach, municipal experience, cost, team, timeline)
A rendered PDF file was produced alongside the Markdown

evals.name: ambiguous-match-uncovered-requirement
evals.prompt: Northfield sent over their analytics RFP (it's at test-rfps/03-northfield-analytics-uncertified-requirement.md). Draft our response please. I want to be able to hand this to our proposal reviewer, so be straight with me about anything you weren't sure about.

Critically, the HITRUST CSF certification requirement (4.3.2) must be flagged as not covered by approved answers rather than fabricated, and surfaced in the closing summary. Priced inside $400k-$850k, addressed to Angela Voss, quoting RFP #NRHS-2026-114.
assertions: Leads with the data-warehouse offering (governed single source of truth), with dashboards/BI included as scope rather than proposing dashboards alone
Does NOT claim Aventra holds HITRUST CSF certification
Explicitly flags the HITRUST CSF requirement (4.3.2) as not covered by approved answers / needing confirmation before submission
The HITRUST gap is surfaced in the closing summary to the user, not only buried in the document body
Names the actual source systems from the RFP (Epic, Workday, Kronos, Premier, Press Ganey)
Addresses the conflicting departmental definitions of 'patient encounters' via governed metric definitions
States a fixed fee inside the stated budget of $400,000-$850,000
Quotes RFP #NRHS-2026-114 and is addressed to Angela Voss
Acknowledges the buyer's stated preference for their existing Azure tenancy
A rendered PDF file was produced alongside the Markdown

evals.name: prescribed-structure-under-budget
evals.prompt: Need our tender for the Cedar Valley water district job - the ITT doc is in test-rfps/04-cedar-valley-mandated-structure-tight-budget.md. Their budget looks tight to me but see what you can do. PDF please.
evals.expected_output: A tender following the buyer's mandated Part A-H structure (NOT the skill's default 12-section layout), including a Part B compliance table covering R1-R11. Matched to mobile-app-suite. Because the $180,000 cap is below the offering's indicative floor, the response should propose a reduced or phased scope at a deliverable price rather than silently squeezing the number, and say what is deferred. Rendered as a PDF, quoting ITT 2026-07, addressed to Derek Nowak.
assertions: Follows the buyer's mandated Part A through Part H structure rather than the skill's default 12-section layout
Part B contains a compliance table covering every requirement R1-R11 with a Fully/Partially/Not Compliant status per row
Matches the request to the mobile-app-suite offering
Total quoted price is at or below the hard cap of $180,000
Explicitly acknowledges that the budget is below full delivery scope and proposes a reduced or phased scope rather than silently squeezing the price
States specifically which functionality is deferred to a later phase
Treats mandatory offline operation (R2) as a first-class part of the technical solution
Names the buyer's actual systems: Cityworks and Microsoft/Entra accounts
Quotes ITT 2026-07 and is addressed to Derek Nowak
A rendered PDF file was produced
Respects the 20-page limit
